## 3 MAI-Gym

Online RL for GUI agents usually requires building a separate system for each platform: environments that reset reliably at scale, an agent loop for every benchmark, a pool of tasks with trustworthy rewards, and a trainer for long multimodal trajectories. MAI-Gym replaces these with one open codebase, organized around a single rollout path that evaluation, data collection, and training all share. [...] Table 6 compares step-wise and window-wise history. Window-wise history yields much higher prefix-cache reuse and substantially lower training token cost, which in turn reduces training update time from 2166.4 to 810.9 seconds, although rollout throughput decreases moderately. Overall, these measurements suggest that window-wise history offers a better efficiency trade-off in our training setup.

#### 4.3.2 Joint RL Beats Expert Merging

We compare joint RL on mobile and computer tasks with a two-stage alternative: training separate per-domain experts and then merging them by weighted parameter averaging [Goddard et al., 2024]. All runs start from the same warm-up checkpoint, and the joint RL run uses the combined training budget of the two experts. [...] Table 6 compares step-wise and window-wise history. #### 4.3.2 Joint RL Beats Expert Merging

We compare joint RL on mobile and computer tasks with a two-stage alternative: training separate per-domain experts and then merging them by weighted parameter averaging [Goddard et al., 2024]. All runs start from the same warm-up checkpoint, and the joint RL run uses the combined training budget of the two experts.

# MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments

Tongyi-MAI

## Abstract

MAI-Gym is an open platform that unifies GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online reinforcement learning training across mobile, computer, and web environments, enabling scalable synthesis of verified tasks and training of a unified 9B agent with state-of-the-art open performance. [...] and challenging tasks, including resettable mocked apps and coherent cross-app worlds with execution-validated task verifiers. Using MAI-Gym, we train MAI-Gym-9B, a unified 9B agent for mobile and computer use, achieving state-of-the-art performance among open GUI agents under 10B parameters: 78.4% on MobileWorld and 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified. Importantly, RL in a mocked train-ticketing app transfers to its real-world counterpart, improving task success on a phys- ical phone from 28.8% to 48.1%. We release the framework, synthesis skills, mocked apps, 2,000 verified tasks, and the model checkpoint to support repro- ducible research and further advances in scalable GUI agent training. [...] Online reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards has driven rapid progress in mathematics, coding, and tool use, but scaling this success to GUI agents remains challenging due to the high cost of interactive environments and the scarcity of realistic training tasks. We introduce MAI-Gym, an open all-in-one platform that unifies GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online RL training across mobile, computer, and web environments. Through a shared rollout pipeline, MAI-Gym ensures consistent agent behavior across evaluation and training, supports ten established benchmarks, and scales to 20,000 parallel environment instances. Beyond scalable infrastructure, MAI-Gym enables automated synthesis of diverse GUI applications and challenging tasks, including resettable mocked apps
